newsitem.title: UK: Med gas oil slumps, fuel oil up on Romanian demand.
newsitem.headline: Med gas oil slumps, fuel oil up on Romanian demand.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products fell on Thursday with the exception of fuel oil which was buoyed by Romanian demand, traders said.
Gasoline eased, tracking crude futures and spot prices in NWE. "The Med is fundamentally a weaker market, so it has to come off otherwise we'd see a false arbitrage (from NWE)," a trader said.
Naphtha was softer after the reopening of Algeria's Skikda oil terminal put pressure on the market.
The port had been closed for over a week due to high winds, delaying at least three naphtha liftings, traders said.
Contract lifters with urgent requirements have effectively doubled up their supplies, having substituted the delayed Skikda cargoes with prompt parcels on the spot market.
"They'll be out of the market until the end of the month," said one trader.
Gas oil fell in line with a dramatic slide in IPE futures but premiums held steady, traders said. They said buying interest in the Med was relatively slack and saw ample supplies of Russian.
A Russian cargo from the Black Sea weas sold at formula -$6.50 fob, and one trader pegged cif values at Nov IPE +$8.
Fuel oil continued its bull run supported by Romanian demand which appears to have been transformed into a deal at $129 cif Romania.
"It looks like they have sorted out the financing and its going ahead," said one dealer. Romania has said it wants to buy up to 1.2 million tonnes of high sulphur fuel this winter.

Low sulphur cracked cargoes corrected after yesterday's 50,50 deal at $133 fob and high fob +$3 with news that the main Med buyer has secured a 48,000 tonne cargo at $135.50 cif Milazzo delivery by November 10.
